transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Larsen (Redwood AE), Alex Chen (Redwood SE), Ibrahim Khan (Head of Compliance, Lynx), Sofia Marquez (Security Eng, Lynx), Markus Vogel (CTO, Lynx EU)

Summary:
Quick security and compliance deep-dive focused on data residency, region pinning, and subprocessors. Customer wants a clear guarantee and testable process that certain data (clinical PII/PHI) never leaves EU regions and to understand Redwood's subprocessors, KMS options (BYOK/HSM), and audit logging capabilities. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs; agreed to run a region-pin test in staging and exchange docs (SOC2, ISO certificate, DPA redline).

Topics covered (brief):
- Data residency requirements (EU-only processing for clinical PHI)
- Region pinning and routing/fallback behaviors
- Subprocessors and where they operate (cloud infra, logging, monitoring)
- Encryption and KMS/BYOK options (customer-owned keys, HSM)
- Audit logs, retention, and export for compliance
- RBAC/SSO provisioning (SAML + SCIM) and tenant isolation

Transcript:
[00:00] Maeve Larsen: Hey all, thanks for joining. Quick intros, and then Alex will run through how we do region pinning and subprocessors.
[00:18] Ibrahim Khan: Hi, Ibrahim here. High level, Lynx needs to ensure EEA clinical data cannot be exported to the US period. So we need details on cross-border processing, subprocessors, and KMS options.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Totally understood. We'll cover both the logical routing — how requests are pinned to eu-west and eu-central — and the controls, e.g. private deploy options. One note, some of the auto-transcribe may garble things like KV cache into "kayv" but I'll try to slow down.
[00:48] Sofia Marquez: Appreciate it. Also want to know whether audit logs or telemetry ever land in a US-managed logging cluster; that's a hard no for us unless it's pseudonymized.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Good callout. For hosted customers, our control plane sits in US/EU control-plane endpoints — the customer can choose region for inference plane. We separate control plane metadata from inference data; however meta and telemetry may flow to SaaS analytics in the US unless we enable EU-only telemetry (we have option).
[01:35] Markus Vogel: Can you be explicit: when you say "inference plane per region" does that mean the model, the tokenized payload, logs, everything? We need the payload and transient KV cache to remain in EU.
[01:50] Alex Chen: Yes. For region-pinned inference the model runtime, KV cache, and generated tokens are processed on EU compute when pinned. Logs we can route — by default some operational logs are retained in the region, but aggregated monitoring may be shipped to a central observability backend; we can opt to keep logs in-region for customers with EU-only requirement.
[02:15] Ibrahim Khan: What's the mechanism for pinning? Is it per-tenant config, per-request header, or per-route policy?
[02:24] Alex Chen: We support multiple: tenant-level config in the Redwood Console and per-request hint header (x-redwood-region: eu-west-1) for apps that need dynamic routing. For strict compliance you'd set tenant-level mandatory pinning to an EU region and lock it via policy, which disables automatic fallback to other regions.
[02:45] Sofia Marquez: Does that lock preclude cross-region fallback if capacity is constrained? We need availability but not at the expense of sovereignty.
[02:55] Alex Chen: You can configure a policy that allows fallback only to other EU regions. The system alerting will surface if capacity is low; we do not recommend enabling US fallback for EU-restricted tenants.
[03:12] Maeve Larsen: To add, for enterprise customers we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated reserved capacity in EU to meet these constraints. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and no telemetry leaves your VPC unless you opt in.
[03:28] Ibrahim Khan: That sounds promising. If we go Private, do we still get SOC2 evidences and Redwood-managed upgrades?
[03:36] Maeve Larsen: Yes — Private deployments come with the same compliance docs; we ship upgrades with a signed patch manifest and maintain a secure update pipeline. We will also share SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate.
[03:50] Sofia Marquez: On KMS, do you support BYOK? We want to control keys for at-rest encryption for EU tenants.
[03:57] Alex Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported on Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we have a managed KMS by default but can enable customer-managed keys via KMS integrations with AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault in EU regions. For HSM-level controls, we can connect to customer HSM via customer network peering in Private mode.
[04:20] Markus Vogel: Are keys ever exported outside EU? Like the key material or encrypted backups?
[04:27] Alex Chen: No — key material can be configured to never leave the customer KMS region. Backups that contain encrypted blobs remain encrypted; decryption requires the key which you control.
[04:37] Ibrahim Khan: Good. On subprocessors, we need a precise list and which functions they perform and where their data centers are. For example, monitoring and logs — is that a third-party?
[04:48] Maeve Larsen: We'll provide the current subprocessor register. Briefly: cloud infra (AWS/OCI/AZURE) in EU regions, log aggregation (PartnerLog — EU clusters available, default US cluster), SSO/identity (Okta, located in EU/US depending on tenant), analytics (Redwood internal analytics, option to disable). We'll tag each with region and function.
[05:10] Sofia Marquez: PartnerLog being default US is concerning. Can you opt for PartnerLog EU-only?
[05:15] Alex Chen: Yes, PartnerLog has EU-only clusters for enterprise customers. It's part of our EU configuration workflow; we'll note that in the subprocessor list.
[05:25] Ibrahim Khan: On legal, we need a DPA that references EU-only processing and SCCs/IDTA if needed. Also we need to understand any subprocessors that are US-based and whether they ever access EEA data.
[05:40] Maeve Larsen: We'll share the DPA and can add contractual commitments about subprocessors and the requirement that certain data classes not be transferred. SCCs are used for any necessary transfers and we support EU model clauses.
[05:53] Markus Vogel: A quick technical question — audit logs: can we get a continuous export of audit logs to our EU S3 bucket and keep them for 7 years?
[06:04] Alex Chen: We support log export to customer-owned buckets in EU for both request/response logs and admin audit trails. Retention is configurable; 7 years is technically feasible but we recommend tiered archival. There are cost implications which we'll outline.
[06:20] Sofia Marquez: Do audit logs contain payload? We can't have PHI in logs.
[06:26] Alex Chen: By default request/response logs are redacted; there's a configurable option to capture full payload only for debugging and only when customer enables it. For compliance you'd keep redaction on and capture metadata only.
[06:40] Ibrahim Khan: What about SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC? We want SCIM and SAML with role mapping and just-in-time provisioning.
[06:49] Maeve Larsen: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and detailed RBAC with tenant + project scoping. Roles are customizable and we produce audit trails when a role change occurs.
[07:02] Markus Vogel: Does the RBAC operate across the control plane and the inference plane? We need to ensure devs in US BU can't flip region pinning.
[07:12] Alex Chen: Controls are replicated: tenant-level policy enforcement is stored in the customer config (control plane) but we also enforce it at the inference gateway so a control-plane misconfig won't silently allow cross-region routing. There is an admin role required to change pinning policy; you can also enable MFA and restrict role changes via IP allowlists.
[07:35] Sofia Marquez: Great. On monitoring/telemetry, what data is considered telemetry? CPU/mem/latency vs token contents.
[07:44] Alex Chen: Telemetry is primarily metrics and traces (latency, token-per-second, memory) — it does not include payload contents unless you enable debug capture. Logs are handled separately and can be in-region.
[07:58] Ibrahim Khan: We also want to test the enforcement. Can you run a pinning test where we send an EU-pinned request and show the trace that proves it processed on EU nodes and no Egress to US services?
[08:10] Alex Chen: Absolutely. Next step is we spin up a staging tenant pinned to eu-central, run requests with an injected trace ID, and show the end-to-end logs and routing decision. We'll redact sensitive payloads but include routing metadata.
[08:28] Maeve Larsen: We'll also provide a short runbook for how to perform the test from your side and sample scripts.
[08:35] Ibrahim Khan: Fine. One more: subprocessors often change — what's your notification policy?
[08:41] Maeve Larsen: We notify customers through the Console and email at least 30 days before adding a new subprocessor and maintain the subprocessor register. For material changes we offer contract rights to object.
[08:51] Sofia Marquez: About contracts: we'd like an amendment that promises EU-only processing for specified classes and remedies if breached.
[08:58] Maeve Larsen: We'll escalate that to legal; we can draft a narrow MSA amendment for data sovereignty commitments.
[09:05] Markus Vogel: Operational question: if we use Dedicated capacity in EU, but Redwood's control plane is global, could someone in the US still see metadata like job names?
[09:17] Alex Chen: Metadata exposure is a function of which control plane you pick. For Dedicated in EU we can provision a regional control plane or offer Private so control plane is customer-managed. If you need zero metadata to leave EU, Private is the recommended path.
[09:32] Ibrahim Khan: Anything about backups? Snapshots of model state or logs?
[09:37] Alex Chen: Snapshots are stored in the configured storage region; we can schedule snapshots to EU S3. Encrypted snapshots require keys; if BYOK is enabled Redwood never has key access.
[09:50] Sofia Marquez: On-chain reference: do you support EEA binding corporate rules or just SCCs?
[09:57] Maeve Larsen: We typically rely on SCCs and SCC-based mechanisms; if a customer requires BCRs we can discuss at legal level but it's not common.
[10:07] Ibrahim Khan: Can we get the concrete list of subprocessors now as an attachment?
[10:11] Maeve Larsen: Yes — I'll attach it after the call. It will include partner function, data category, region, and the legal basis for transfer.
[10:19] Sofia Marquez: Quick clarification: what about ephemeral GPU instances that might autoscale to a different region temporarily?
[10:27] Alex Chen: Autoscaling honors the region pin: ephemeral instances are provisioned in the pinned region or a sister EU region if policy allows. We do not autoscale into non-EU regions for pinned tenants.
[10:40] Ibrahim Khan: Are there exceptions where an engineer in US could access logs for debugging?
[10:46] Alex Chen: Access is logged and requires approved access. For Private deployments you can keep logs inside your VPC and we won't access them. For Hosted/Dedicated, we have an internal access request workflow with attestations and time-limited access; every elevation is captured in admin audit logs.
[11:05] Markus Vogel: Will you include a sample audit log showing an access elevation?
[11:09] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include a redacted sample.
[11:14] Ibrahim Khan: Any change management windows for Private? We need patching windows and notification.
[11:20] Maeve Larsen: Yes, Private customers get a maintenance calendar and signed patch manifests. Urgent security patches may be applied earlier with customer consent except for zero-day criticals where we advise immediate action.
[11:33] Sohia... sorry Sofia: Are there SLA penalties if a region pin is violated?
[11:38] Maeve Larsen: Contractual remedies are negotiable; in practice we encode pinning in infra and test regularly. Breaches would trigger incident response and contract remedies per the DPA/MSA.
[11:50] Ibrahim Khan: Ok, that helps. Let's recap next steps.
[11:53] Maeve Larsen: Recap: we will share SOC2 & ISO certs, the subprocessor register with EU cluster mappings, a runbook and infra diagram for region pinning, and schedule the staging pin test. Customer will send data class list with PHI flags. Legal to follow on DPA redlines.
[12:12] Markus Vogel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
